title: PS5 Controllers
video_prompt: Create a 30-second vertical tech short about PS5 controllers. Open on the DualSense, unveiled April 7 2020 and launched with PlayStation 5 on November 12 2020 in the US, Japan, and other first-wave markets. It weighs about 280 grams and measures about 160 by 66 by 106 mm. Voice-coil actuators in the grips can make wind and sand feel like they hit your hands. Motors in L2 and R2 add resistance, like a bowstring tightening, and players can reduce those trigger effects or switch them off. Share became Create. A built-in microphone and mute button work without a headset. USB-C replaced micro-USB, Bluetooth 5.1 handles wireless play, and a 3.5 mm jack takes a headset. The original pack has a 1560 mAh battery that charges in about three hours from the console. A light bar sits on the touchpad edges, and five LEDs mark your player number. DualSense Edge launched January 26 2023 at $199.99 with replaceable sticks, back buttons, and adjustable triggers. The Access controller launched December 6 2023 at $89.99 with four 3.5 mm ports and a layout that works at any angle. Tone: fast, tactile, documentary. End on: Fact or whack?

title: Cheapest Versus Quality
hook: The $67 controller is the quality one.
video_prompt: Create a 30-second vertical tech short about PS5 controller prices versus quality. Open on a white DualSense at $66.95 on Walmart, against a $74 list price on PlayStation Direct, both checked October 21 2026. Access controller is $89 and DualSense Edge is $199 on PlayStation Direct. Amazon shows the Edge at $189.05. Days of Play 2026 hit $54 and that sale is over. Sony says PS5 games play with a DualSense, and officially licensed PS5 pads are the other route. An unlicensed bargain pad costs less and misses PS5 games. The $67 DualSense keeps grip haptics, adaptive triggers, the mic, and the touchpad. IGN's February 2026 guide still names it the best overall PS5 controller. The Edge keeps that same feel, then adds back buttons and replaceable sticks, with about 5 to 6 hours of battery. Triple the price buys paddles or drift-proof sticks. The DualSense feel stays on the cheaper pad. Tone: blunt, buyer-advice, fast. End on: Fact or whack?
